sources.entry: Nim: _Writing a stow alternative to manage dotfiles_

summary.title: Day 6: Manage your dotfiles easily with nistow
summary.one_liner: You learn how to build a GNU Stow-style dotfile manager in Nim that symlinks config files from an app directory into a destination (home by default) using command-line parsing and directory walking.
takeaways: Dotfiles are organized as <app>/.config/<app>/file, and stow links each file relative to a destination directory such as the home directory.
getopt is used to parse long and short options like --app, -a, --dest, --verbose, --simulate and --force.
walkDirRec with yieldFilter={pcFile} collects every regular file under the app directory, and the path prefix is replaced with the destination.
The stow procedure creates parent directories and symlinks each file, with simulate, verbose and force modes controlling behavior.
summary.summary: This Nim Days post (Day 6) builds a small stow clone called nistow for managing dotfiles. It defines the expected directory layout (an app folder containing .config/<app>/ files), then walks through a CLI entry point that parses options with getopt, defaults the destination to the home directory, and reports errors. The core logic uses walkDirRec to map each source file to a destination path, and a stow proc that creates directories and symlinks, honoring simulate, verbose and force flags. Full source is linked on GitHub.
